June 21, 1944 - B - b 
Three and four years ago, when the first bans were placed upon the 
extremist movements on the left and the right, political circles in

essential for us to muster all our forces with a view to insuring our

17. Sep. 1940 
Ladies and Gentlemen, 
Inspite of the tremendous battering which 
continues over Great-Ãritain, North-Western Europe and the 
Mediterranean, the diplomatic battle is gaining in intensity. 
The fact that no decision seems in view in the military field, 
stimulates the efforts of both camps to gain fresh fields of 
action and new allies. 
Thus we can discern a new effort made by 
the Axis-Powers to bottle-up the Mediterranean. Inspite of 
Italy's successes around Abessynia and Egypt, the transfer of 
new British forces, intended for the defence of the Suez Canal, 
could not be prevented. These reinforcements arrived to a large 
extent through the Straits of Gibraltar, and the Axis's wooing

Monday Bulletin, October 23, 1939 
Ladies and Gentlemen, 
You are not unaware of the role played in contemporaneous European 
affairs by the propaganda of the major states. In fact, the importance of 
this role could scarcely be exaggerated. One of the reasons for this is 
that these campaigns are not assigned objectives which are only political 
in nature. They are not simply an effort to justify, in the minds of the 
state's own citizens, and, at the same time, in the minds of citizens of 
other states, the territorial or economical aspirations and ambitions 
of the country which launches them. 
No, this propaganda also has a moral, spiritual, and intellectual 
import, and aims at the conversion of as many people in as many countries 
as possible to definite, politico-economic doctrines, a number of which 
have come into favor the last fifteen years. [...]

Ladies and Gentlemen, 
Last week the federal government released for publication a series 
of "instructions for the civil population in-case of war." This act on

Monday Bulletin, December 18, 1939 
Ladies and Gentlemen, 
Lest week I endeavored to explain, before this microphone, Switzerland's 
position with regards to the League of Nations. I reminded you of how our 
country, after twenty years of differential neutrality, during which she was 
bound by the obligations of the pact to participate, with the other members of 
the League, in the application of economic sanctions, resolved to return to 
her traditional conception of foreign policy on the basis of complete 
neutrality. This decision was recognized by the League, and Switzerland was

The Swiss Confederation is a democracy of a special nature. Its constitution 
grants citizens - as do the constitutions of other democratic states - a number 
of clearly defined liberties, such as freedom of faith and conscience, freedom 
of the press, and the freedom to organize political parties. In the majority of 
the cantons that make up the Confederation, Swiss citizens elect their parliaments 
and their governments. And in addition to this power of election, the 
Swiss people have the right to decide changes in constitution and law. This last 
privilege is the most vital characteristic of Swiss democracy. As a matter of

Switzerland and the right of asylum 
A somewhat uneasy feeling was created recently in Switzerland when 
the American and British foreign departments requested our government 
to refuse certain persons the right of asylum in Switzerland, should 
this privilege be asked for. They said, in fact, that to grant such 
an entrance would be considered an offence against the principles for 
which the United Nations are fighting. We heard later that a similar 
request, was sent to six other neutral countries. It seems that these

infringment upon our sovereign rights. Every independent State, whether 
great or small, must be able to decide for itself when it is to grant

After the capitulation of Italy, about 2o,ooo Italian military and civil 
refugees and some l,ooo escaped Allied prisoners poured into Switzerland. This 
naturally created problems which had to be dealt with by the competent ministry of 
Justice and Police. 
Federal Councilor de Steiger has given a detailed report in parliament about 
this refugee influx. Switzerland now has nearly 60,000 emigrants and refugees within 
her borders, which represents 1 - % of her entire population. This would mean, 
for England, half a million people, and for the United States 1 and a half million.

Does it sound thoughtless and light-hearted to think of war - which carries 
in its wake so much horror and distress - as a means of education ? And yet

SWISS BOOKS COME INTO THEIR OWN

The two great book-furnishing countries of Switzerland, Germany and France, can practical ly no longer be reckoned with. In Leipzig the large publishing houses and

THE EIGHTIETH ANNIVERSARY OF THE GENEVA CONVENTION 
In all simplicity, an anniversary is being celebrated at Geneva at 
this end of Augusts that of the 80 years of the Red Cross. Who does not 
know the emblem of the Red Cross ? It is, for millions of suffering human 
beings, the symbol of humanity. 
80 years ago, on the 22 August 1864 to be exact, the first Geneva 
Convention was enacted by a diplomatic conference called at Geneva by the 
Swiss Federal Council. The convention gave legality to the great principles

abstract:
When the war is over! 
October 1, 1944--B b. 
We, Swiss, have noted with lively interest the passage in President 
Roosevelt's speech   his first electoral speech   in which he stated 
that his opponents' claims that United States troops would not be demobilized 
at the close of hostilities for fear of unemployment were not true to 
fact. In Switzerland, too, the question as to what will happen when the 
soldiers return to their homes again is up for discussion. It has been, in 
point of fact, for some time already. Yes, just what will happen when the 
soldiers go back to work at a time when industry and agriculture will no 
longer be working for war economy? Will unemployment get out of control? 
Well, Federal Councilor Kobelt, head of the Military Department, has 
just dealt in detail with this great problem in a speech before parliament. [...]

ties that unite Holland and Geneva. The Netherlands, especially in the 17th

SCIENCE -- ART -- EDUCATION
June 26, 1945 -- FE --b.
===============================
TWENTY-FIVE YEARS OF STUDENT SOCIETIES
The Unio of Swiss Student Associations is celebrating, in connection
with the "Fourth Swiss University Convention", twenty-five years of exis-
tence. This Union, to which belong all students of Swiss nationality in
the confederation, was a creation of post-war times of the first world
war, and was designed to insure all students in our universities a certain
self-government along democratic lines and to provide financial facilities 
for needy students. In the course of its development, the Union has done
